roadintro: Priority order, not a release calendar. Refer to the application roadmap for dependencies and acceptance criteria.
vision.intro: A small workshop and a multinational distributor both need reliable records, but their workflows differ. We want them to share business concepts without sharing a database, a cloud provider or a single prescribed way of working.
architecture.intro: Independent services own business rules, data and migrations. Published contracts let an extension integrate without writing into another service’s database.
industries.intro: One platform, many contexts. A product, lot or order can have shared identity while a future industry package supplies validated attributes, units and policies. These examples are design questions, not available packages.
community.intro: You do not need to code. Tell us what happens when a customer orders ten units and only six are available. Who decides what to ship, and what must the next shift know? Use a fictional example.
contribute.intro: Most software projects already have established structures when you join. At erp4us, you can help define them. You don’t need to code to contribute.
hero.stage: We’re building the foundations, not shipping a finished ERP. Join now to help decide how it should work.
mission.label: Our mission
mission.title: The world deserves a better ERP.
mission.intro: Organizations should control their business records, choose where they run their software, and adapt their processes without depending on a single vendor.
mission.control.title: Your business. Your data.
mission.control.text: Use open standards and interfaces so organizations can move and integrate their data on their own terms.
mission.community.title: Decisions in the open
mission.community.text: Make proposals, trade-offs and decisions visible so contributors can challenge and improve them.
mission.foundation.title: Built to be maintained
mission.foundation.text: Give services clear responsibilities and use tested contracts so teams can change them independently.
mission.international.title: Across industries and borders
mission.international.text: Bring together people who understand different workflows, languages and local requirements.
mission.statement: We’re not just building software. We’re building an alternative.
founding.title: Become a founding contributor.
founding.note: Small contributions are welcome and there’s no time commitment. Founding contributor means joining early, not special voting rights, ownership or equity.
area.engineering.intro: Run the Rust and Angular quickstart and report friction. API contracts, business logic and tests all need review.
area.architecture.intro: Bring a concrete example that challenges a domain boundary, data model or event contract.
area.domain.intro: Describe an exception from manufacturing, logistics, accounting, purchasing, sales, inventory or quality using fictional records.
area.design.intro: Sketch an enterprise workflow and its failure states, or review keyboard navigation and accessibility.
area.infrastructure.intro: Review Compose reproducibility, CI checks or recovery assumptions. Use the security policy for private reports.
area.infrastructure.link: Look at the CI quality baseline
area.automation.intro: Describe a workflow suited to automation and where a person must approve it. Discuss MCP and agent boundaries.
area.docs.intro: Translate an instruction, review a tutorial or clarify business vocabulary for contributors and users.
governance.intro: GitHub is where we work. The project is in bootstrap governance: maintainers triage, review and document decisions. No additional account or platform is needed.
onboard.requirement: Bring a requirement or an example to Discussions. Use synthetic data and describe what should happen, including exceptions.
onboard.issue: Check for an existing issue before filing one. Agree on the outcome and acceptance criteria before starting.
onboard.decision: For architecture changes, compare options and trade-offs in public; maintainers record accepted decisions as ADRs and explain deferrals or rejections.
onboard.review: Open a scoped pull request linked to the issue. Include tests and the required DCO sign-off. CI supports, but does not replace, human review.
onboard.conflict: Discuss disagreements on their merits, disclose conflicts of interest, and follow the code of conduct. Maintainer nominations are based on sustained contribution, review and conduct, with public feedback.
development.intro: Track what has changed and see how people contribute. GitHub is the source of record.
human.title: People lead. AI can assist.
human.intro: People set the architecture and own the outcomes. Coding agents can help implement scoped issues with explicit acceptance criteria and repository-specific instructions.
human.review: Automated tests and CI make changes easier to review; ADRs record why decisions were made. Humans remain accountable for review and approval. Contributions made without AI are equally welcome.
stack.activeNote: Engineering work focuses on the first order-to-procurement workflow. An end-to-end business workflow is not available in the local preview.
stack.discussionNote: Product and material models, international operations and agent boundaries are open for input.

principle.source: Open source · inspect and adapt first-party work under Apache-2.0.
principle.community: Community-driven development · discuss requirements in public.
principle.data: Data sovereignty · keep control of business records.
principle.hosting: Self-hosting · begin with a local Compose setup.
principle.modules: Modular architecture · let each service own its rules.
principle.language: Internationalization · separate language from business identity.
principle.api: Open APIs · publish and validate service contracts.
principle.agents: Agent-native architecture · use the same authorized commands.

stack.heading: Technology stack
stack.localNote: Today you can register and retrieve an article. This is a local demo for synthetic data, not a production-ready ERP.
stack.angular.name: Angular and TypeScript
stack.angular.detail: The browser workspace registers and retrieves articles through the HTTP API. Typed forms and shared components help keep validation and interactions consistent.
stack.rust.name: Rust, Tokio and Axum
stack.rust.detail: The Master Data service checks article registration rules and serves article lookups. Rust gives the service explicit types and errors, while Tokio and Axum handle asynchronous HTTP requests.
stack.mongodb.name: MongoDB
stack.mongodb.detail: Master Data owns its database. A transaction saves the article and its pending event together, so a failed event write cannot leave an article without its registration event.
stack.contracts.name: OpenAPI and JSON Schema
stack.contracts.detail: Published contracts describe HTTP operations and payloads so clients can integrate and validate data without reading a service’s database.
stack.compose.name: Docker Compose
stack.compose.detail: Starts a repeatable local environment for Master Data and MongoDB without requiring a Kubernetes cluster.
stack.nats.name: NATS JetStream
stack.nats.detail: An optional local demo delivers article registration events to a separate receipt service. JetStream can redeliver messages after interruptions; the consumer prevents duplicate receipts.
stack.planned: Planned, not available in the preview
stack.identity.name: OpenID Connect (OIDC)
stack.identity.detail: A self-hostable identity provider is planned for real sign-in; ERP services will still check tenant access and permissions. The local demo uses a demo token instead.
stack.storage.name: S3-compatible object storage
stack.storage.detail: The planned Documents service keeps file contents in private object storage and manages metadata and business references separately.
stack.kubernetes.name: Kubernetes and Helm
stack.kubernetes.detail: Deployment options for operating services independently after migration, isolation and recovery procedures have been validated.
stack.mcp.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
stack.mcp.detail: A planned gateway will let agents discover approved tools and call the same authorized business APIs as users. Running erp4us will not require an AI provider.
